candidates.title: 6 people injured after vehicle strikes pedestrians at festival in Saint-Tite, Que.
candidates.description: The incident happened on Saint-Joseph Boulevard in Saint-Tite, Que. on the site of the Festival Western de Saint-Tite, a major attraction for the region that is wrapping up this weekend. All six pedestrians are expected to survive.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Family of Bhishma Rajyaguru, killed in crash with Sask. Roughrider, mourns his death
candidates.description: Bhishma Rajyaguru's father and sister remember him after he died when ​Saskatchewan Roughrider​ Jayden Dalke crashed into his vehicle.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: If most Albertans don't want to leave Canada, where is the pro-Canada movement?
candidates.description: Over the last year, a steady drumbeat of polling has found again and again that most Albertans oppose separation — but based on fundraising and online chatter, you might not know that.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: There might be no economic case for expanding the Port of Churchill, but that may not be the point
candidates.description: The question before Manitobans right now is why Canada and Manitoba are not simply proceeding with a $3-billion port expansion and railway upgrade, if indeed a Hudson Bay shipping route is essential for Canadian sovereignty.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Mounties can now choose not to wear a name tag. A Halifax defence lawyer says that's a problem
candidates.description: A Halifax lawyer says an RCMP policy change that means officers are no longer required to wear name tags on their uniforms while on duty poses a threat to police accountability and transparency.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: GlobalEye surveillance plane under the microscope as Conservatives call for twin probes
candidates.description: Federal Conservatives want the auditor general and parliamentary budget officer to investigate Ottawa's planned GlobalEye purchase, questioning whether proper procurement rules were followed. The demand follows revelations the Saab aircraft meets only some military requirements and that competitors had not been shown those requirements before the government announced its preferred aircraft.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: CRA still owed over $5B in COVID-19 benefits sent to ineligible recipients
candidates.description: Ottawa is still owed $5.56 billion of outstanding debt related to COVID-19 benefits sent to those who were later deemed ineligible, according to data the Canada Revenue Agency provided to CBC News.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Top cyclists from around globe descend on Montreal for road racing world championships
candidates.description: For eight days, beginning Sept. 20 through the 27th, the city’s historic cobblestone streets in the old port and the iconic Mount Royal will be transformed into hundreds of kilometres of cycling circuit as athletes from around the globe fight to become the next road cycling world champion.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: There’s a lot of talk about changing Quebec’s voting system. Why hasn’t anything been done?
candidates.description: The first-past-the-post system is once again under scrutiny by some political parties and voters in the province. For years, there's been talk of changing it to make the province’s election results more representative of its population.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Family wants answers after death of injured woman sent home from Saskatoon hospital
candidates.description: The family says Kirsten Hanke, 30, died due to blood clots after a broken ankle she suffered in August went untreated for more than a week.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Michigan tourist who posted about wearing 'Lake America' sweatshirts to Halifax says it was AI
candidates.description: A CEO from Michigan has cut her trip to Halifax short after she says she's received death threats over a viral Facebook photo where she and three family members appear to be wearing "Lake America" sweatshirts.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Former Saskatoon Christian school principal found guilty of assaulting 3 students with paddle
candidates.description: A Saskatoon jury found former Saskatoon Christian school principal guilty on three counts of assault. Duff Arthur Friesen, 68, the former principal of a private Christian school was accused of assaulting five former students with a weapon — a wooden paddle.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Calgary council divided on whether city should take official stance on Alberta separatism
candidates.description: Mayor Jeromy Farkas said he anticipates bringing urgent business or calling a special meeting for city council to debate whether to take an official stance on the upcoming Alberta independence referendum this fall. But some councillors argue the debate is outside their jurisdiction.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney government files 3rd court challenge in First Nations child welfare complaint
candidates.description: The Carney government has filed its third court challenge in a year as a longstanding fight with First Nations organizations over the future of their communities' child and family services continues. Canada is challenging the Canadian Human Rights Tribunal's latest ruling in the nearly 20-year-old case.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Norval Morrisseau masterwork not seen for 40 years unveiled at Thunder Bay Art Gallery
candidates.description: After 40 years in storage, a rare masterwork by Ojibway artist Norval Morrisseau has been unveiled at the Thunder Bay Art Gallery in northwestern Ontario. The painting is on loan from EA Studios Calgary, and is described as "very spiritual" and "very powerful."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Really need to rethink this': Manitoba wrong to choose daylight over standard time, sleep experts say
candidates.description: Scrapping twice-yearly time changes in Manitoba is a great move, but staying on daylight time instead of standard time is the wrong choice, says a sleep medicine expert — especially for students.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Never giving up': Alberta separatist leaders say referendum vote won't end their fight
candidates.description: Premier Danielle Smith and her government expect next month's separation referendum to be the last word on the subject — but those fighting for an independent Alberta say no matter the outcome, the fight goes on.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: No horseplay by the hole: Crews rescue horse stuck in mud pit near Melfort, Sask.
candidates.description: It took a couple of tries, but a crew of firefighters from Melfort managed to free a horse from a deep pit of mud outside the city this week.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russian drones are stalking Ukrainian trains and trying to hobble the country's rail system
candidates.description: In recent weeks, Russia has stepped up drone strikes on Ukraine's rail network, targeting trains and the approximately 20,000 kilometres of track that form a key transportation artery across the country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico say journalists denied access to White House after Trump ban
candidates.description: Reporters from three major news organizations — CNN, MS NOW and Politico — were denied access to the White House on Saturday, a day after President Donald Trump said he was barring them because of reporting he found to be "fake news."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Greenland, Denmark say deal with U.S. will not cede sovereignty
candidates.description: Denmark and Greenland on Saturday said any agreement with the United States would not compromise Greenland's sovereignty, after President Donald Trump said the deal would give Washington "permanent control" over the Arctic island's security, leaving its precise scope unclear.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada won't pay directly into EU budget under Carney's plan: ambassador-designate
candidates.description: As Prime Minister Mark Carney presses toward creating a "unique alliance" with the European Union, Canada's ambassador is ruling out paying directly into the 27-nation bloc's budget.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israel moving ahead with settlement plans that would split West Bank in two, rights group says
candidates.description: Rights groups say the Israeli government is forging ahead with a contentious settlement expansion plan that would effectively divide the occupied West Bank, long criticized as a threat to the viability of a future Palestinian state.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says deal struck to boost U.S. military presence in Greenland
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said Friday he has a deal with Denmark to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland after months of threatening to take island by force from the NATO ally.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump announces White House ban on CNN, other media outlets
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump announced an immediate White House ban on a number of news outlets, including CNN.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's top general is up for a senior NATO post. Will Trump get in her way?
candidates.description: Canada's Gen. Jennie Carignan faces Germany's Gen. Carsten Breuer on Saturday in a secret-ballot contest to chair NATO's Military Committee. A victory would make Carignan the first woman to hold the post and return Canada to the chair after nearly two decades, amid Ottawa's push for deeper ties with Europe.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Former Pakistani PM Imran Khan’s son says he fears for his father's life behind bars
candidates.description: Kasim Khan, the the son of jailed former Pakistani prime minister Imran Khan, says he wakes up most mornings expecting to learn that his father has died in prison.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror breaks silence, says he didn't have 'any doubts' of her guilt
candidates.description: The lone juror who wanted to convict Lindsay Clancy of murder for killing her three children said he was certain of her guilt, but that other jurors wouldn’t listen to him, according to a statement released by his lawyer Friday in his first public comments on the case.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Germany's far-right AfD party is taking pages out of Trump's playbook
candidates.description: From creating a deportation task force to revising history lessons in schools, the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, which won a resounding victory in the state of Saxony-Anhlat last week and could soon hold power, wants to implement policies that echo some of those enacted by U.S. President Donald Trump.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: ICE agent pleads not guilty to lying to FBI about shooting of man in Minneapolis
candidates.description: The top prosecutor from Minnesota's Hennepin County announced the arrest Friday of an ICE officer charged for shooting a Venezuelan-born man in January at the height of a deadly immigration blitz launched by the Trump administration.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Indonesian divers recover 3 bodies from capsized ferry as salvage operation begins
candidates.description: Rescue teams in Indonesia on Friday recovered three bodies from a capsized ferry while preparing to salvage the wreckage of the accident, bringing the confirmed death toll to nine, with 126 people still missing, officials said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: At least 21 killed in Pakistan mosque bombing near police station
candidates.description: A vehicle bomb exploded Friday at a mosque near police offices in northwestern Pakistan as gunmen tried to storm the compound, killing at least 21 people and wounding 80 others, police and rescue officials said. Among those killed and wounded were police officers attending prayers at the mosque.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: F-16 crashes during training in Michigan; pilot ejects safely
candidates.description: An F-16 pilot safely ejected before the fighter jet crashed Thursday in rural Michigan, sending plumes of smoke into the sky and triggering temporary evacuations for nearby residents after police said hazardous chemicals spilled from the wreckage.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Philippines school shooting leaves 2 students, gunman dead
candidates.description: Three students were killed in a school shooting in the southern Philippines on Friday, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman who turned the gun on himself, provincial officials said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New cat species identified for the 1st time in a century
candidates.description: A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia's cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living cat species has been formally named and described in more than a century.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russians begin voting in parliamentary election set to cement Kremlin's power
candidates.description: Russians on Friday began three days of voting in the country's first wartime parliamentary election, which features virtually no opposition and is all but certain to secure the Kremlin's political dominance.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. import ban on Canadian molasses highlights sticky sugar industry feud
candidates.description: The Trump administration's announcement of a ban on importing Canadian molasses left some scratching their heads. The ban, set to hit on Sept. 29, has resurfaced allegations of sugar smuggling and a battle between North American sugar giants.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Rogue AI swarm used a University of Toronto link-shortening tool to communicate
candidates.description: A swarm of rogue OpenAI agents that hijacked a German website in the spring reportedly also used at least 10 other websites for unsanctioned communications earlier this year, including a link-shortening tool at the University of Toronto.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Gas prices are dropping. You can thank the 'winter blend' for that
candidates.description: After ticking up earlier this week, gas prices dropped by about eight cents overnight, and could fall by a few more by the weekend according to one expert. But diesel is soaring, which could be bad news — even for those who don't drive.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nato welcomes Greenland deal as Trump says it will give US 'permanent security control'
candidates.description: Denmark and the US have reached an agreement after months of threats from Donald Trump to annex the territory.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Houthis claim attack on Saudi capital after smoke seen rising near Riyadh airport
candidates.description: The King Khalid International Airport incident caused hours of flight disruptions and comes amid an escalating conflict with Houthi rebels in Yemen.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
candidates.description: The AI model accessed the internet and guessed credentials to three websites, a Google official told the BBC.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Grim discoveries of murdered women spark fear in South Africa
candidates.description: Dineo Motapane is one of nine recent victims whose deaths have left a nation traumatised over the level of violence against women.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Shark attack prompts rare kill order in Western Australia as victim named
candidates.description: Greg O'Neill "loved the ocean", his family say, as police boats and helicopters patrol Perth's beaches in search of his body and the shark that attacked him.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: At least 21 killed after vehicle loaded with explosives rams Pakistan mosque
candidates.description: A four-year-old child is among those killed in the attack, during which gunmen also opened fire on a police facility.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Kerry Kennedy: 'It would be a tragedy' if Kennedy Center is demolished
candidates.description: The BBC’s Caitríona Perry spoke to the late president's niece, as protesters gathered at the venue to condemn demolition threats.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: I found love at an Irish matchmaking festival - and I want others to do the same
candidates.description: Mary Timby flew to Ireland on a whim last year and met her boyfriend at a matchmaking festival.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Tata Sons: India's corporate crown braces for upheaval amid boardroom revolt
candidates.description: The Tata boardroom battle has intensified over a re-appointment of its chairman and a diktat to go public.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Canadians dream of Europe as Carney floats longshot plan for living and working in EU
candidates.description: Torontonians are excited by the possibility of moving to the EU, even if it is unlikely anytime soon.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: This Olympic river has 500 crocodiles in it - but that's not the main concern
candidates.description: Queensland's Fitzroy River has been selected for the 2032 Games, despite concerns over the course - and its inhabitants.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Enough is enough': Women protest after string of murders near Johannesburg
candidates.description: The police have since set up a task team to investigate the murders and have urged women in the Kempton Park area to avoid walking or running alone "particularly in isolated areas".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Is the Kennedy Center losing 'hundreds of millions of dollars'?
candidates.description: Records in 2024 show the venue had a surplus of millions of dollars once contributions and grants had been factored in.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Trump says ban on some news outlets is 'because they're fake news'
candidates.description: The US president on Friday announced he is "immediately" banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Would Australians support a smart glasses ban?
candidates.description: As Australia considers barring the use of smart glasses in government offices, the BBC asks people in Sydney what they think.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: See tiny organisms on show in microscopic video competition
candidates.description: The winning video features tiny hair-like structures, called cilia, in the airways of a child with a rare genetic disease.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Move faster to solve climate challenges, Prince William says
candidates.description: The Prince of Wales tells the BBC we need to "accelerate" in finding solutions to climate challenges as Earthshot nominees are unveiled.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: France, Poland and European allies warn of escalating Russian 'hybrid' attacks
candidates.description: The leaders of France, Poland, and other leading European nations are alarmed over what they describe as Russian "hybrid" attacks.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Life in Kabul 5 years after the Taliban's return
candidates.description: Five years after the return of Taliban rule, NPR visited Kabul to see how Afghans are dealing with their new government's strict social restrictions.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Russia holds parliamentary vote in areas it seized from Ukraine in the war
candidates.description: Russia's parliamentary election for the first time is being held in Ukraine's regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the start of its full-scale invasion more than 4 1/2 years ago.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: As Europe warms, Italy sees West Nile virus spread
candidates.description: Italian health authorities see evidence that rising temperatures and longer warm seasons are helping mosquitoes spread West Nile virus across a wider area, during more months of the year.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. and Denmark reach deal to build U.S. military presence in Greenland
candidates.description: President Trump says he has a deal with Denmark to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland. The announcement comes after months of threatening to take the island by force from the NATO ally.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Russians head to the polls to choose lawmakers for their parliament
candidates.description: Russians head to the polls to choose lawmakers for their parliament, the Duma. It's Russia's first nationwide parliamentary race since launching its full scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: When Trump and Xi meet they will discuss AI. 'Track Two' talks are already buzzing
candidates.description: An informal network of dialogues at think tanks and universities is bringing together experts from the U.S. and China to talk about the shared perils of AI — and possible paths forward.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Will even one of the U.N.'s 17 'sustainable development goals' be met by 2030?
candidates.description: The 17 goals agreed upon by world leaders are incredibly ambitious. Are we even close to achieving any of them? If we don't, is the project a failure?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Judge says Trump can't demolish Kennedy Center. And, lawsuits target voter intimidation
candidates.description: A federal judge ruled yesterday that President Trump cannot tear down the Kennedy Center without a 30-day notice. And, recent lawsuits seek to keep armed federal officers away from polling sites.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Ever wonder how the Fed's interest rate actually works? We've got answers
candidates.description: The Federal Reserve just raised interest rates this week for the first time this year. So how does it actually work? And what does it mean for the economy — and the rest of us? Here are some answers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How a pizza app changed our relationship with waiting
candidates.description: Status trackers are ubiquitous on online apps and ordering. We have the story the seminal Domino's Pizza Tracker that led to many copies, and we check on why many of the trackers now aren't accurate.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
candidates.description: The president chalked the ban up to what he called unfavorable coverage, and he threatened that bans on other media companies could be coming.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Ms. Rachel has entered her album era, and she is so happy about it
candidates.description: Ms. Rachel has conquered YouTube, Netflix and the toy aisle. Now she's making an album, with real instruments, big feelings and her littlest listeners in mind.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
candidates.description: Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after serving in the role for more than 50 years. His son, Howard, will become Berkshire Hathaway's new chairman
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
candidates.description: A bacterial infection is wiping out Florida's citrus trees. Growers hope a rootstock developed with gene-editing technology could keep the disease at bay.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A bad year for the crypto industry just got a lot worse
candidates.description: The cryptocurrency industry just suffered a major defeat in a bill they had badly wanted to get through the Senate. It's the latest setback in a terrible year for the sector.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Betel nuts are a top mind-affecting substance. Now there's evidence of ancient use
candidates.description: New research on ancient human remains suggests the habitual usage of betel nuts, a plant seed with mind-affecting properties that is popular in parts of Asia despite the health risks it presents.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Doctors raise concerns about views and experience of members on federal task force
candidates.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. names new members to powerful federal task force that plays a key role in determining the kind of preventive case people get. In a major departure, the new members of the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force include specialists instead of experts on preventive care and general medicine, raising fears among many doctors.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: To prevent deaths in childbirth, Kenyan moms turn to an AI powered chatbot
candidates.description: Many questions come up during pregnancy. Is swelling normal? Are avocados safe to eat? For folks in Kenya who don't have a search engine at their fingertips, a chatbot is offering a lifeline.
candidates.author: NPR
